alternatives.benefit: Could directly help learners understand why their answer was wrong.
alternatives.cost: May not address feeling dumb or leaving if tone is the main problem.
alternatives.label: Explanation-first
alternatives.undo_cost: Likely low; explanation content could be revised without changing the whole quiz flow. Assumes learners primarily need clearer reasons.

alternatives.benefit: Could reduce the feeling of being dumb and make learners more willing to continue.
alternatives.cost: May feel supportive without making the underlying mistake clearer.
alternatives.label: Tone-first
alternatives.undo_cost: Likely low; wording could be changed without a major rebuild. Assumes emotional response is the main cause of leaving.

alternatives.benefit: Could address both understanding and the feeling of leaving smarter.
alternatives.cost: More design and content work, with possible added cost or overengineering.
alternatives.label: Explanation and tone together
alternatives.undo_cost: Moderate; separating or reducing the combined treatment may require revising question feedback. Assumes both concerns materially contribute.

supports.quote: what I actually want is learners leaving a wrong answer feeling smarter not dumber.
it has to work on phones because thats where most people use it.

framings.text: Socratink should help learners understand a wrong answer and leave feeling smarter rather than dumber, while working on phones and keeping no gamification. The AI tutor is only a possible route; cost, chatbot fatigue, explanation versus tone, and the unverified question-4 drop-off remain open.

candidate.outcome: Learners who get something wrong understand why and leave feeling smarter rather than dumber; the experience works on phones and does not use gamification.

questions.text: When learners get something wrong, should the first fix prioritize explaining why, changing the tone, or both?
